title: Sound of the old brass bands
summary: Old brass bands had no saxes but many clarinets and alto horns; Thomas says the instruments blended, with strong trumpets drowning the softer ones.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Who played what: early band size and instrumentation

blocks.x: Uh, I was thinking about brass bands, but I wanted to ask you, um, those old brass bands, did they, did they, they must have sounded a little different than the brass bands they have now, didn't they? Did they have a lot of saxes in them then, like they have now?

No, they didn't have no sax, that, uh, they did, I mean, I don't remember them having no sax, but they, I know that they had a lot of those, I hear people call them pick horns. Yeah, an owl horn, or something like Old Man Barbarian played. That's right, yeah, they had a lot of them, and clarinet, they had more than one clarinet player. Did you ever play E-flat clarinet?
On a little shortness? I never did, never did.
Well that must have made quite a, a little different sound there for a brass band.

Well, it, in a way, it did, you know, but you know a lot of instruments playing together, well, sometimes you can't tell that there's too much different in the sound because they all, they all blend together. Because, especially if they got strong trumpet players, and strong trombone players, and then a strong trumpet might drown out the software instruments, you know, to a certain extent. Yeah. So you couldn't tell.
